From: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@finservco.com>

Cc: security@finservco.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unusual token activity detected — need IR plan + artifacts

Camila,

Quick heads up from our platform security team — we observed a burst of anomalous API token usage tied to the API key provisioned for FinServCo between 2026-10-20 23:40 UTC and 2026-10-21 00:05 UTC. No customer data exfiltration has been confirmed on our side yet, but we need to run a joint investigation.

Can Redwood provide: 1) your incident response plan (IRP) for API key compromise scenarios; 2) a short timeline of mitigation steps you intend to take; and 3) forensic artifacts (request logs, token issuance history, IP/TLS handshakes) for the 25-minute window cited above. FinServCo is SOC 2 scoped and we need this packet for our compliance review.

We appreciate a quick pointer to where we can review the IRP and an expected ETA for the artifact delivery.

Thanks,
Sam Hayes
Director, Platform Security
FinServCo

- Acknowledged the alert and rotated the API key tied to FinServCo at 2026-10-21T08:15-07:00 (rotation performed; old key disabled).
- Spinning a forensics job to pull request logs, TLS metadata, and key issuance records for 2026-10-20T23:30Z–2026-10-21T00:10Z.
- We'll provide a redacted artifact bundle and a summary IR timeline within 4 hours, and a full manifest and SOC-2 evidence export within 48 hours.

I'll attach the Redwood Incident Response Summary and a one-page mitigation timeline in the next note.

- Camila

Adding technical details and what we'll hand over. Sam — here's the scope of the artifact bundle we're preparing:

- Request-level logs (nginx access logs + app-level request_id tracing) for the 40-minute window around the spike.
- API key issuance and rotation history (KMS key records + Vault audit trail).
- Short-lived TLS session metadata (SNI, cipher suite, originating IPs) and reverse DNS where available.
- Runtime host logs for GPU workers that served requests (container stdout/stderr sampling).
- Kubernetes pod metadata for any pods that reported errors during the window.
- Checksums and a CSV manifest (forensic_manifest_20261021.csv) plus a short MD5/SHA256 file for download verification.

We will redact customer payloads but preserve metadata needed for your internal correlation. Delivery plan: temporary GCS staging link with access tokens (valid 48 hours) by ETA 12:30 PM PDT (2026-10-21T12:30-07:00). If you need longer retention for compliance, let us know and we will arrange secure transfer.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Thanks Camila/Neha — that scope looks good. A few clarifications from our side:

- We will need IPs and TLS metadata preserved in original form (no anonymization) for our network forensics team.
- Please include any rate-limiting or WAF events that occurred around the spike; those may have blocked follow-on activity.
- Can Redwood confirm whether the old API key (now disabled) was in use by any internal tooling or other customers at the time? If so, list the service accounts.

We do not require payload contents, only metadata, but the original conntrack/tcpdump packet capture (or a subset) would be very helpful if feasible.

Sam
